questions.question: I'm buying — compare Milford and Takapuna Central on zoning capacity and flood exposure.

quality.note: Thoroughly grounded with correct per-layer citations, consents-vs-completions distinction, no combined risk figure, and full hazard caveat, though slightly long.

anthropic.answer:
On zoning capacity (weighted more heavily in Buying mode), Takapuna Central is notably higher at 52.7% {{c8}} versus Milford West's 10.3% {{c2}}, suggesting considerably more intensification headroom under the AUP. However, Milford West's consenting rate of 19.7/1,000 dwellings {{c3}} outpaces Takapuna Central's 8.7/1,000 {{c9}}, meaning actual build activity is currently stronger in Milford West — both figures measure consents issued, not completions.

On flood exposure (also weighted more heavily in Buying mode), Takapuna Central carries a significantly higher floodplain figure at 49.11% {{c7}} versus Milford West's 23.67% {{c1}}, and Milford West's overland flow path density of 18.48 km/km² {{c4}} is notably denser than Takapuna Central's 8.18 km/km² {{c10}}. Coastal inundation runs the other way: Milford West shows 4.89% {{c5}} (rising to 6.92% with +1m sea level rise {{c6}}), while Takapuna Central is lower at 0.85% {{c11}} (2.09% with +1m {{c12}}). These are separate council model layers with different vintages and should not be combined into a single exposure figure.

In summary, Takapuna Central offers much greater zoning capacity, but carries higher floodplain exposure; Milford West has stronger recent consenting activity and lower floodplain risk, but faces more coastal and overland flow exposure on other layers. The preference shaping this emphasis was Buying mode (zoning capacity ×1.5, flood exposure ×1.5, consenting rate ×1.5).
